scope: Review whether newly surfaced Binary DXF parser/encoder tools provide independent evidence and reconcile peer implementation lineages with the existing DWG/DXF parity plan.

method.kind: Public package documentation, project repository metadata, and local plan reconciliation
method.evidenceBoundary: Package and repository metadata establish advertised API scope and dependency classification only. The dxfscan test source was not inspected, so this pass does not claim its tests call dxfbin. No parser output, writer output, semantic correctness, or native application behavior was executed.

observed: The published ISC crate documents a binary-DXF-only R13+ parser with a typed subset, lookup indices for layers/styles/blocks/handles, an Entity::Unknown case, and no_std compatibility.
Docs.rs package metadata lists dxfbin ^0.1 as a development dependency.
The repository page currently lists one commit and no GitHub release.
No source/test inspection established whether the dev dependency is used for fixture generation or tests.
doesNotEstablish: full OBJECTS, owner, XDATA, proxy, opaque-tag or unknown-record preservation
malformed-input safety or exact behavior across all listed entities
that dxfscan tests use dxfbin or that their outputs are invalid as independent evidence
evidence.planUse: If a future composed check selects dxfscan, pin the crate checksum and matching source revision, inspect the exact test/development-dependency usage, feed it libdxfrw-emitted binary output where useful, and compare parser results with an independently authored literal manifest. Do not count a dxfbin-to-dxfscan pipeline or shared generated expected data as independent evidence.

observed: The ISC crate documents streaming text-DXF to Binary-DXF conversion without interpreting drawing structure.
Its typed sink classifies group-code values into strings, booleans, integers, doubles, and binary chunks, and emits the Binary DXF sentinel.
The docs expose a 0.1.0 release and no drawing-entity model or parser API.
doesNotEstablish: DXF graph, owner, block, or handle closure
independent validation of Binary DXF output
DWG support or native application acceptance
evidence.planUse: No dependency or test lane is needed. If used in a separate transport experiment, validate the encoded bytes through an independent decoder and externally authored expected group/value data.

observed: Existing primary sources maintain distinct DXF parser/projection routes, older read-only DWG projection routes, and DWG readers with shared ancestry.

uncad identifies LibreDWG as its DWG path and undxf as its DXF path; ACadRust downstream applications share that codec lineage; codelibs/libdxfrw identifies itself as a fork in the same libdxfrw code family.
These source relationships support the plan's existing lineage matrix; project wrappers, converters, renderers, and apps are not automatically independent parser votes.
evidence.planUse: Retain the current route matrix and use only the smallest optional peer set that adds a missing direction/version/entity route. Keep local format-specification or independently authored expectations as the ground truth.

nextActions: Continue existing fast local slices; do not install or run these peer crates during ordinary implementation.
At a composed binary-DXF checkpoint only, select dxfscan only if an exact source/package pin adds useful coverage beyond already available routes.
Before any dxfscan result is scored, inspect its pinned dev/test dependency path and use independent literal expected values; dxfbin is an encoder/transport helper, not a parser or oracle.
Keep Binary DXF syntax/field decode separate from graph closure, ACIS semantics, kernel validation, and application acceptance.
Keep J256, J260, J268, J284, J293 and J295 DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting.
